title: SIU probing death of gas-theft suspect in Chatham-Kent
article: Ontario's police watchdog is investigating after a suspect in a gas-and-dash theft died after a roadside encounter with a Chatham-Kent OPP officer.
Police closed a section of Highway 401 east of Chatham while the Special Investigations Unit began its probe July 7 of the deadly "interaction" between the unidentified man and the officer.
The officer fired his pistol, the SIU confirmed, but neither the agency nor the OPP would say if the suspect was shot.

Chatham-Kent OPP responded at about 4:30 a.m. July 7 after a theft was reported at a gas station between London and Chatham near Highway 401. An officer was following the suspect's car when it left the road and rolled into a ditch near the Highgate exit, the SIU said.
"An interaction took place with a male occupant and the officer discharged his pistol," the SIU said.
The man, whose identity hasn't been released, later died in hospital, the SIU said.
An SIU spokesperson declined to say whether the case could be classified as a police-involved shooting.
An OPP spokesperson referred all inquiries to the SIU.
Police closed a section of Highway 401 in both directions between Victoria and Orford roads, near Ridgetown, about a 30-minute drive east from Chatham, for a criminal investigation, the OPP said.
Traffic was backed up for hours as drivers were forced to detour on side roads before lanes were reopened just before 5 p.m.

The most recent fatal police shooting in Southwestern Ontario happened on Dec. 3, 2019, when two Huron County OPP officers shot and killed Wade Vanderwal, 44, after he charged at them with an axe outside of his home in Exeter.
The SIU cleared both officers, who fired 11 shots at Vanderwal.
The SIU probes all shootings, serious injuries and allegations of sexual assault involving police.
It asks anyone with information or video evidence of the July 7 incident to contact investigators at 1-800-787-8529.
